solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Rodent attack by the sound of it (6)

indicators.note: tells you to take the letters from how the phrase is said, not spelt

blocks.note: to go for someone is to attack them

annotation.surface: A rodent turning on someone, or at least seeming to.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words GO FOR run together into one burrowing animal; a gopher is a North American ground squirrel.
annotation.definitionFit: Named by example: the gopher is a North American burrowing rodent, a pocket gopher or ground squirrel.

indicators.note: the letters of POINT are formed into a new order

annotation.surface: Advice on whittling a stick to a sharp point.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'sharpness' as a pointed stick; here it means sharpness of mind.
annotation.definitionFit: Gumption is practical good sense, the quick-wittedness called sharpness.

entries.clue: Tails of sheep, all vets praise (8)

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: last letters of sheeP and alL
to vet is to check over, to audit

annotation.surface: A vet at a farm, admired by all for handling the sheep's tails.
annotation.walkthrough: 'vets' looks like animal doctors among the sheep, but it is the verb: checks carefully.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: plaudits are applause and acclaim, so praise in the plural sense of many voices.

entries.clue: In advance, close to the leader’s left (5)

indicators.note: the leader (first letter) has left, so it goes

blocks.note: NEARLY loses its first letter N

annotation.surface: A runner almost level with the front-runner, drawing ahead on the left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the direction but 'has gone': the leader of NEARLY departs.
annotation.definitionFit: To arrive early is to arrive in advance of the time.

blocks.note: room, as in room to manoeuvre

annotation.surface: A chance to make snowballs once the snow has turned to slush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snowball' is not the ball of snow but the verb: grow fast, as a rolling snowball does.
annotation.definitionFit: To snowball and to mushroom both mean to grow rapidly.

annotation.surface: A junior putting forward an idea to the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'present suggestion' reads as offering an idea; 'present' is the adjective, now.
annotation.definitionFit: An undercurrent is a hidden hint or suggestion of feeling.

blocks.note: a maiden voyage is the first one

annotation.surface: A young woman being chased by someone careless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'maiden' is the adjective of a maiden speech or voyage: first.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: diving in without looking, head leading, is acting without caution.

blocks.note: a bloomer is a flower, here the iris

annotation.surface: A gangland boss making a colossal blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake beside the mob boss; it is something that blooms. Osiris is the Egyptian god of the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Osiris ruled the underworld in Egyptian myth.

indicators.note: TA is taken inside the other word

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks

annotation.surface: A religious convert quietly acknowledging gratitude.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's 'convert' is a new believer; the definition is the verb, change form. MU(TA)TE.
annotation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change, to convert into another form.

indicators.note: MERE blocks AG in, surrounding it

blocks.note: mere = pure, as in 'the mere thought'
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Tiny ingots of pure silver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'blocks' looks like a noun, silver bars, but is the verb: ME(AG)RE.
annotation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty, very small in amount.

blocks.note: notions are ideas, one of them read singly here

annotation.surface: Airy romantic ideas typed up as a bulleted slide.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer splits in two: ideas set out as bullet points form a kind of list, which is the romantic's stock-in-trade.
annotation.definitionFit: A romantic, as a noun, is an idealist who sees the world as it could be.

blocks.note: from boxing, where a low punch breaks the rules
where are trousers worn? Under the waistband

annotation.surface: Someone caught not wearing trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not sporting trousers' pictures a missing garment; 'sporting' is really fair play, and the second half asks where trousers go.
annotation.definitionFit: A below-the-belt remark is unfair, not sporting, from the boxing rule.

entries.clue: Sleeping companion in bed ate dry crackers (5,4)

indicators.note: crackers = crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: Someone eating dry crackers in bed with their partner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits being eaten; it is the adjective, mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is what a child takes to bed.

indicators.note: one who dictates says words out loud, so his FAINT is heard, not spelt

annotation.surface: A tyrant's flimsy trick.
annotation.walkthrough: The dictator is not a tyrant but someone dictating, speaking so another writes: FAINT spoken is heard as FEINT.
annotation.definitionFit: A feint is a pretended move to deceive, a ruse.

entries.clue: Published piece works best with guile (12)

blocks.note: a book that is out is published
a chess piece is a man
an oeuvre is an artist's body of works

annotation.surface: A writer's published article judged the craftiest of their output.
annotation.walkthrough: 'best' reads as an adjective, finest; here it is the verb, beat.
annotation.definitionFit: To outmanoeuvre someone is to get the better of them by cunning.

entries.clue: Dancers’ movement or horses circling finally evoke what for Degas? (9)

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it, so ARABS go round the E
take the last letter of evoke

blocks.note: Arabs are a breed of horse
que is French for what, and Degas was French

annotation.surface: Degas painted ballet dancers and racehorses; which does the painter want to capture?
annotation.walkthrough: Degas is only there to signal French. ARAB(E)S + QUE.
annotation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a ballet position on one leg with the other extended behind.

entries.clue: Graduate brought in to study disease protection (8)

indicators.note: something brought in to a place ends up inside it, so MA ends up inside PONDER

blocks.note: MA = Master of Arts, a graduate

annotation.surface: A graduate recruited to research an illness.
annotation.walkthrough: PO(MA)NDER. A pomander, a ball of spices, was carried in the belief it warded off plague.
annotation.definitionFit: Pomanders were once carried to ward off infection.

indicators.note: HOARSE is said, and heard as HORSE

annotation.surface: A swimmer with a deep, rough voice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deep' and 'gravelly' both seem to describe the voice; 'Deep' is the noun, the ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: A seahorse is a small upright-swimming fish.

blocks.note: to perfect a skill is to master it
to pet an animal is to stroke it

annotation.surface: An ideal pet doing something clever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perfect pet' reads as adjective and noun; both are verbs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stroke of mastery is an inspired act, a move only a genius would make.

entries.clue: Uplifting part for a gifted baritone (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means reading bottom to top, backwards
the answer is only part of the phrase

annotation.surface: A rousing role written for a talented singer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a role, which suits Figaro, but it signals the hidden word. Figaro is a baritone role in Mozart and Rossini.
annotation.definitionFit: Figaro, in The Marriage of Figaro and The Barber of Seville, is sung by a baritone.

entries.clue: Keep replacing sulphur as temperature lowers (6)

indicators.note: one letter is swapped for another
T comes in as the replacement for S

blocks.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur; it goes

annotation.surface: Instructions to keep swapping out sulphur as the temperature falls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'lowers' reads as the verb, brings down; it is the noun, things that low (moo). CASTLE with T for S.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: 'lowers' as a noun means things that low, and cows moo, or low.

indicators.note: the phrase carries the answer inside it

annotation.surface: An engineer lugging an empty tin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Empty' seems to describe the tin, but it is the definition, as in an empty remark.
annotation.definitionFit: Inane means empty of sense, silly.

entries.clue: His unit measures speed merchants, flying (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters take off in a new order

annotation.surface: Speed merchants in flight having their speed measured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'speed merchants' reads as a unit, fast drivers; 'speed' belongs to the definition. Flying fits, since Mach numbers are aircraft speeds.
annotation.definitionFit: Ernst Mach gave his name to the Mach number, speed relative to the speed of sound.

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be seen within it, so A sits within TWIN

annotation.surface: A writer's piece printed twice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'article' seems to be a newspaper piece by the writer; it is the grammatical article A. TW(A)IN.
annotation.definitionFit: Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn.

entries.clue: Old stuff of note found in an endless search (8)

indicators.note: TI is found inside the rest
SEARCH's synonym QUEST loses its last letter

blocks.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
search = quest, without its end letter

annotation.surface: Hunting for a valuable old object in a search that never ends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'of note' reads as notable, but 'of' only links; the note sits between the two other parts.
annotation.definitionFit: Antiques are old things valued for their age.

indicators.note: take the first letter of late

annotation.surface: A race that starts at the end of summer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who does sums. A ladder is a run in tights or stockings.
annotation.definitionFit: A ladder is a run, a line of broken stitches in hosiery.

entries.clue: Dish the Spanish must slice to mete out (8)

indicators.note: EL cuts into the other letters
the letters of TO METE are put out of order

annotation.surface: A Spanish cook who must cut a dish up to share it out.
annotation.walkthrough: OM(EL)ETTE: EL slices into the rearranged letters of TO METE. Fittingly, a Spanish omelette is a tortilla.
annotation.definitionFit: Named by example: beaten eggs cooked in a pan make one kind of dish.

entries.clue: English racecourse lacking a current course (6)

indicators.note: AINTREE goes without A and I

blocks.note: Aintree, near Liverpool, hosts the Grand National
lose A and I (the symbol for electric current)

annotation.surface: An English racecourse missing a stretch of its current track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'course' appears twice: first the racecourse, then the meal course that is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in Britain an entrée is a dish served between the main courses, in America the main course itself.
